requirements.text: Make sure the related incident reflects this update in its work notes, noting that follow-up and tracking will now be managed through the primary incident

cells.worknotes: LIKE '%INC-000061%' OR worknotes LIKE '%INC_061%' OR worknotes LIKE '%primary%'

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_090' AND (worknotes LIKE '%INC-000061%' OR worknotes LIKE '%INC_061%' OR worknotes LIKE '%primary%')
assumptions: the related incident is INC_090 (the child); its seed worknotes value is 'Check.', so the note must name the primary incident by number, by id, or as 'primary'
the three alternatives are one disjunctive predicate on worknotes (a list would mean all must hold); the sql wraps it in parentheses

disagreement: worknotes predicate: A a disjunction (number, id or 'primary') with IS NOT NULL and <> 'Check.' alongside, B LIKE '%primary%' alone; chose A's disjunction because the request fixes the gist, not the wording, and a note naming INC-000061 by number without the word 'primary' satisfies it, which B's predicate would reject; A's IS NOT NULL and <> 'Check.' dropped as implied by the LIKE predicates
no benchmark check covers the work note

requirements.text: so that INC-000061 is treated as the primary record
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM child_incident WHERE parent_incident = 'INC_090' AND child_incident = 'INC_061'
assumptions: boundary of the relationship's direction: a link the other way round (INC_090 as parent) must not be created

requirements.text: so that INC-000061 is treated as the primary record (its own parent stays unset)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_061' AND parent_incident IS NULL
assumptions: boundary of the relationship's direction: the primary record must not itself be made a child of INC_090 (parent_incident is NULL on the seed)
disagreement: parent_incident predicate: A = 'INC_090' expected 0, B IS NULL expected 1; chose B because both are right and IS NULL is tighter (it also catches any other parent being set)

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on the five benchmark checks (all kept), the on-hold change with its SLA pause (TSLA_027, policy section 6), the notification (NOTIF_031 to the caller USER_027), the child_incident link (CINC_007, INC_061 parent) and INC_090's parent_incident, and on the reverse-link stay.
disagreement: worknotes predicate on INC_090: A a disjunction (INC-000061, INC_061 or 'primary') plus IS NOT NULL and <> 'Check.', B LIKE '%primary%' alone; chose the disjunction because a note that names the primary incident by number is a correct outcome B's predicate would reject; the redundant IS NOT NULL and <> 'Check.' dropped (logged on the requirement).
disagreement: stay on INC_061's parent_incident: A = 'INC_090' expected 0, B IS NULL expected 1; chose B's as the tighter of two right predicates (logged on the requirement).
Acting user USER_039 (Karen Watkins) is admin with full CRUD, so no permission rule halts the task. The two created rows (one notification, one child_incident link) are anchored by next-in-sequence ids; the benchmark's checks for them had no id anchor, so the requirements are stricter only in the id. update_incident is the only listed tool that writes incident.worknotes.
